items.t: Putin says Russia won't negotiate with Ukraine after bridge strike
items.m: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia will not negotiate any limited ceasefire now with Ukraine, citing a Ukrainian strike on a highly symbolic bridge this week.

items.t: Ukraine's NATO membership is relevant for European security, Macron says
items.m: BERLIN, Nov 19 - French President Emmanuel Macron said the question of NATO membership for Ukraine was \"relevant\" for European security, given the country's strong and well equipped army.

items.t: Netherlands summons Russian ambassador as Kyiv embassy hit
items.m: Nov 19 - The Dutch government summoned the Russian ambassador in the Netherlands on Thursday, after the Dutch embassy in Kyiv suffered minor damage when a projectile landed near the building.

items.t: European leaders reject 'Yalta 2.0' for Ukraine after Trump meets Putin and Xi
items.m: "A Yalta format will not bring peace," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said at the end of a Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin just hours after Trump, Putin and Xi held talks in China.

items.t: Trump Flaunts Camaraderie With Xi and Putin but Has Little to Show for It
items.m: President Trump called Russia’s leader his “friend” and marveled at China’s warm welcome for his first-ever trilateral summit. But there were no breakthroughs on nuclear control, the war in Ukraine or A.I.

items.t: Prince Harry says he is ready to rejoin British Army if needed amid Russia-Ukraine war
items.m: Prince Harry has said he would be willing to rejoin the British Army if the need arose, amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. The Duke of Sussex made the remarks during an unannounced visit to Ukraine, where he warned that Europe should be concerned about the growing threat from Russia. Harry served 10 years in the Army, completing two tours in Afghanistan as an Apache helicopter pilot.
